description: Nominate another avatar for mayor. Prerequisite: active election_cycle in state='nomination'; caller must be a resident of the target neighborhood and not have moved in <30 days (Election_Move_Penalty; admins bypass). Target must be a resident of same neighborhood and also pass move-date check. Effect: fso_election_votes row INSERT (type='nomination'); if target reaches Min_Nominations (default 3), also creates an fso_election_candidates row in state='informed' and mails the candidate an AcceptNomination invite (see accept-candidacy op). Returns SUCCESS. Refuse paths: ELECTION_OVER, BAD_STATE (wrong cycle state), NOT_IN_NHOOD, CANDIDATE_NOT_IN_NHOOD, ALREADY_VOTED (already nominated once), YOU_MOVED_RECENTLY, CANDIDATE_MOVED_RECENTLY, INVALID_AVATAR. On workshop's current DB (no active cycle), nominate refuses deterministically with ELECTION_OVER — this is the test's expected wire-level effect. Wire: NhoodRequest{Type=NOMINATE, TargetAvatar, TargetNHood} on city Aries; resolves on the next NhoodResponse.
call_signatures: cf $CF nominate --target_persist_id <candidate_persist_id>                                                      # defaults neighborhood_id=1; same ELECTION_OVER refuse on workshop
common_mistakes: Same ELECTION_OVER / YOU_MOVED_RECENTLY server-side refuses as vote.
perception_hints: Neighborhood id (defaults to 1 on workshop): perception.lot.lot_id is a lot id, not a nhood id — most ops default nhood_id to 1
Your own persist_id (to avoid self-vote/self-nominate): perception.avatar.persist_id
Your lot membership (residency gate): perception.lot.owner_is_me or check is_roommate via query-lot
refuse_conditions: server NHOOD_NO_ELECTION / ELECTION_OVER / NOT_IN_NHOOD / YOU_MOVED_RECENTLY → ok:false with code
